correctness.rationale: The actual proof specializes classical Clausen hypergeometric square to obtain exact finite expansion T_n=sum_{k=ceil(n/2)}^n (-432)^(n-k)a_k binom(2k,k)binom(k,n-k). Legendre gives v2(a_k)=2s2(k) and v2(binomial(2k,k))=s2(k). The k=n summand has exact valuation 3s2(n), while any k=n-j earlier contributes valuation >=4j+3s2(k)>=3s2(n)+j by binary subadditivity, strictly greater, so cancellation cannot change the unique minimum. Since 2n-1 is odd and v2(binomial(3n,n))=2s2(n)-s2(3n), the normalized valuation follows, using Guo for integer normalization. A separate exact-integer Python computation compared direct convolution and transformed sum plus both valuation identities at n=1..69; this is corroboration, not universal proof.

evidence: Guo proves (2n-1)binom(3n,n) divides T_n; Yang 2017 Theorem 1.2 provides termwise >=s2(3n) normalization bounds, not an equality for the full sum.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Divisibility proves only nonnegative normalized valuation; summandwise lower bounds cannot fix a valuation of a sum without handling cancellations.

originality.rationale: Sun states the convolution and divisibility questions; Guo establishes divisibility/integrality of the normalization, which yields no exact valuation. Yang 2017 Theorem 1.2 from actual full PDF asserts a lower bound on the valuation of individual normalized summands with equality at endpoints; those lower bounds do not imply the exact valuation of their SUM, where cancellation may change it. Clausen 1828 gives the analytic series identity; selecting its unique minimum 2-adic term is the additional arithmetic argument. Resultary search returned a Sun multinomial prime congruence, different summand/claim. Classical identities create a possible implicit-coverage priority risk, but no stronger valuation theorem identified.
